parties: D-Link Holding Mauritius Inc (acquirer) / D-Link India Limited (target)
headline: D-Link Holding Mauritius files SEBI takeover disclosure for D-Link India stake consolidation
sum: D-Link Holding Mauritius Inc, the ultimate holding company, has filed mandatory SEBI Regulation 31(4) and 31(5) disclosure with NSE signalling a substantial acquisition or consolidation of shareholding in D-Link India Limited. The filing indicates the acquirer has crossed a prescribed threshold of voting rights and must disclose acquisition price, acquirer background, and funding sources within the statutory timeframe.
implication: Parent company consolidation triggers mandatory open offer or delisting requirements under SAST 2011; practitioners must verify whether this is a threshold-crossing disclosure, a precursor to compulsory tender offer, or a route to delisting under Regulation 37(b).
detail: D-Link Holding Mauritius Inc, as ultimate holding company of D-Link India Limited, has filed a Regulation 31(4)–(5) disclosure under the Substantial Acquisition of Shares and Takeovers Regulations 2011. This filing signals either a fresh substantial acquisition crossing 25% threshold or consolidation of existing voting interests. The disclosure must include acquisition price per share, acquirer's background, funding sources, and proposed end use of funds. This is a material corporate action requiring stock exchange notification and public disclosure within 4 working days of triggering event.

framework.note: Mandatory disclosure of substantial acquisition crossing 25% or acquisition of more than 5% in 30 days; must disclose acquirer, price, sources and end use.
Triggers compulsory open offer if threshold crossed; Regulation 37(b) permits exemption for acquisition by existing promoter.
Preferential allotment framework if any share issuance involved in consolidation.
Exchange-level notification and timing requirements for filing and public disclosure.
If parent company seeks to delist subsidiary post-consolidation of 90%+ voting rights, applies from date of approval by shareholders.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act 1999, Schedule I
framework.note: If D-Link Holding Mauritius acquisition involves FDI or repatriation; RBI approval route applicable if non-resident investor.
Exemption for share acquisition under scheme of amalgamation; may apply to consolidation if restructured.

conditions: Acquisition must cross 25% voting threshold or 5% acquisition within 30 days to trigger Regulation 31 disclosure
Acquirer background and identity verification by stock exchange
Funding source declaration (internal accruals, borrowing, issuance, or sponsor support)
Public disclosure within 4 working days of triggering event
approvals: NSE/BSE notification (mandatory filing under Listing Rules Chapter VIII)
SEBI confirmation of threshold crossing (implicit in disclosure acceptance)
Open offer or exemption determination (if voting rights cross 25% or consolidation exceeds slab)
Stock exchange advisory/approval on disclosure form and timing
structure.novel: Consolidation by existing ultimate holding company; practitioners should clarify whether acquisition is a fresh fresh share purchase, inter-corporate subscription, or in-specie transfer of shares by parent.

triggers.note: Threshold crossing or substantial acquisition within 30 days triggers mandatory disclosure within 4 working days.
If voting rights reach or cross 25%, compulsory open offer at floor price required unless exemption applies.

triggers.law: NSE Listing Rules, Chapter VIII Section 3
triggers.note: Stock exchange receives disclosure form and verifies completeness and timing; publicity requirement applies.

firms.note: No legal advisors named in primary filing; typical for parent company consolidation filing.
